newsitem.title: UK: UK expands "guest beer" scheme in breweries' pubs.
newsitem.headline: UK expands "guest beer" scheme in breweries' pubs.

text.p: Britain's government on Thursday laid an order before parliament proposing an extension to the existing rights of landlords of "tied" pubs to offer their customers guest beers.
Under present rules, one guest cask-conditioned, or "real" ale can be offered in every pub owned by a brewery.
The change, announced by Consumer Affairs Minister Nigel Griffiths, will mean tenants can offer a "bottle conditioned" beer produced by another brewer as well.

"Small brewers will have an extra opportunity to market their products and I am satisfied that extending the guest beer provision would not undermine the tied pub system in the UK," Griffiths said in a statement.
